title: Iran Claims Strike on U.S. Radar in Bahrain; No U.S. Confirmation Yet
excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike in Sirik. Washington and Manama had not commented, and the claim is unverified.
body:
• Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Friday they targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain — a claim, not a confirmed strike.
  • The Guards said the move retaliated for what they described as an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik county in southern Iran.
  • There was no immediate comment from the United States or Bahrain, and the claim could not be independently verified.
  • Reuters described it as Iran's first such claim of an attack on American military assets in a Gulf country since early September.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday it targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain, according to Iranian state media — the first such claim of an attack on American military assets in a Gulf country since early September, Reuters reported.

The Guards said the strike was in retaliation for what they described as an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Iran's southern Sirik county, in Hormozgan province, according to Iranian state media cited by Reuters. The Associated Press, in a report carried by Reflector, said Iran's official IRNA news agency quoted the Guard as saying the attack followed a U.S. strike on a telecommunications pole in the southern Iranian port of Sirik, and that the Guard described the radar as destroyed.

No U.S. or Bahraini confirmation

There was no immediate comment from the U.S. or Bahrain, Reuters reported. U.S. Central Command and Bahrain's Ministry of Information did not immediately respond to requests for comment, according to the Associated Press. Neither the radar claim nor a second claim by the Guard could be independently verified, AP said.

Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet and has been one of the strongest critics of Iran, AP noted. The Guard's statement said the attack on the radar was a serious warning to the U.S. to cease its strikes, according to AP.

Second claim in the Strait of Hormuz

The Guard also said a liquefied petroleum gas tanker struck a mine, causing an explosion, while trying to sail through the Strait of Hormuz, according to IRNA as reported by AP. The Guard said the vessel ignored repeated warnings while transiting the eastern part of the strait. That claim also could not be independently verified, and there was no immediate report of the incident from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, a British military agency that monitors incidents at sea, AP said.

Context: a fragile lull

The claim came amid a fragile lull in the conflict between Iran and the U.S., which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 and has since spread across the region, Reuters reported. Iran launched missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases in Gulf states and sought to restrict shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies, while Washington imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, according to Reuters.

Until the United States or Bahrain confirms damage, casualties or an interception, the Bahrain radar incident should be treated as an Iranian claim made during an ongoing conflict, not as an established strike.
